crm_rows.title: Live Más Open and Live Más LIVE: turn Peacock viewers into known fans
crm_rows.what_happening: Taco Bell produced the Live Más Open celebrity golf tournament (played Nov 2, streaming on Peacock Nov 20 and airing on Golf Channel). Earlier it premiered its Live Más LIVE menu reveal show on Peacock. Both reach national audiences well beyond the in-person guests.
crm_rows.why_flowcode_fits: Streaming and broadcast viewers are anonymous to Taco Bell. An on-screen code can link a viewer to a sign-up or app download and show which show and which market drove it.
crm_rows.suggested_play: Your Live Más Open golf special streams on Peacock on Nov 20 and airs on Golf Channel, after Live Más LIVE premiered on Peacock in March. You likely cannot tell which viewers came from the shows or what they did next. Put a dynamic Flowcode on screen that opens a FlowHub with the app download, a Rewards sign-up and a first look at the secret menu items shown at the event. Use a different code per show and airing so the destination can change as the menu changes. You would see scans by show and market, new Rewards sign-ups and app installs tied to the broadcast. Flowcode result: ESPN College GameDay collected 32,000 emails in one day from a broadcast code. How are you measuring what viewers do after they watch your Peacock shows today?
crm_rows.would_measure: Scans per airing and platform, app installs and Rewards sign-ups from the code, and secret-menu page views.

crm_rows.title: Flamin' Hot launch and puffer jacket giveaway: bring in-store customers into the drop
crm_rows.checks_passed: f1_touchpoint; f2_digital_action; f3_matches_play; i1_scale_stated; i2_national; i3_live_or_upcoming
crm_rows.what_happening: Taco Bell brought back the Flamin' Hot Grilled Cheese Burrito, launched the Flamin' Hot Mini Taco Salad, and is giving away 200 puffer jackets through the Nov 17 Rewards Tuesday Drop.
crm_rows.why_flowcode_fits: The giveaway is app-only while the launch is in restaurants nationwide. A code on in-store materials connects menu buyers to the drop and measures how many enter.
crm_rows.suggested_play: Your Flamin' Hot Grilled Cheese Burrito and new Mini Taco Salad are on menus nationwide, with 200 puffer jackets going to Rewards members on the Nov 17 Tuesday Drop. Customers buying the new items likely do not all know about the giveaway or have the app. Put a Flowcode on in-store posters and packaging that opens a FlowHub with the drop entry and app sign-up. You would see which restaurants and which menu item prompted entries and new app sign-ups. How do you currently get in-store customers into your app drops?
crm_rows.would_measure: Scans by restaurant and placement, giveaway entries, and new app installs from the code.

crm_rows.title: Menu tests (Cantina Carne Asada, Avalanche Taco Trio): in-store feedback codes
crm_rows.what_happening: Taco Bell is testing seven new items at select restaurants in three states, including a six-item Cantina Carne Asada menu in Nashville and Minneapolis-St. Paul and the Avalanche Taco Trio in Tampa.
crm_rows.why_flowcode_fits: Limited tests need quick customer feedback from specific restaurants. A code on test packaging or table cards links feedback to the exact market and item.
crm_rows.suggested_play: Your Cantina Carne Asada test began Nov 12 in Nashville and Minneapolis-St. Paul, and the Avalanche Taco Trio is at select Tampa restaurants. You likely rely on sales data and social posts to judge reactions. Put a Flowcode on the test-item wrapper and sauce packet that opens a FlowHub with a short rating form and a Rewards sign-up. You would see feedback by item and market and which testers joined Rewards. How do you collect customer feedback on test items today?
crm_rows.would_measure: Scans and ratings by test item and market, plus Rewards sign-ups from testers.

crm_rows.title: Redesigned app and Tuesday Drops: drive installs and Rewards sign-ups from physical touchpoints
crm_rows.what_happening: Taco Bell redesigned its app in August with My Menu, My Mods, a new loyalty hub and a Tuesday Drops section. Rewards members earn 10 points per $1, and weekly drops like the Pretty Pink Picnic Kit run in the app.
crm_rows.why_flowcode_fits: Taco Bell has a stronger app and loyalty offer, and in-restaurant and on-pack spaces can bring in new members. Codes at those places show which ones drive installs and first orders.
crm_rows.suggested_play: Your redesigned app launched in early August with My Menu, My Mods, a new loyalty hub and a Tuesday Drops section. Many people in your restaurants and on your packaging likely do not use the app yet. Put Flowcodes on cups, bags, tray liners and counter signage that open a FlowHub showing this week's Tuesday Drop with a one-tap install or Rewards sign-up. Personalize the hub by location or loyalty tier through FlowID. You would see installs and sign-ups by restaurant and touchpoint, and which codes produce first orders. How do you currently credit in-store promotion for new app members?
crm_rows.would_measure: Scans by restaurant and placement, app installs, new Rewards sign-ups, and Tuesday Drop participation.

crm_rows.title: Sauce packet recycling: make the packet a doorway to Rewards
crm_rows.checks_passed: f1_touchpoint; f2_digital_action; f3_matches_play; i1_scale_stated; i2_national; i3_live_or_upcoming
crm_rows.what_happening: Taco Bell and TerraCycle run a U.S. sauce packet recycling program open to all brands. They report one million packets collected over five years, and Rewards members can earn bonus points by registering their recycling email.
crm_rows.why_flowcode_fits: The program asks people to match an email address across two systems. A code on the sauce packet could make joining one scan instead of a manual step.
crm_rows.suggested_play: Your TerraCycle sauce packet program has collected one million packets over five years, and Rewards members can earn bonus points by registering the same email. Sign-up likely depends on people finding and following instructions on their own. Print a Flowcode on the sauce packet that opens a FlowHub explaining recycling and linking the program email to a Rewards account. You would see how many packets lead to registrations and how many Rewards members join the program. Flowcode result: LOVE CORN had 62% CRM conversion and 27k new customers from a packaging QR. How many Rewards members have linked their recycling email so far?
crm_rows.would_measure: Packet scans by region, recycling registrations, linked Rewards accounts, and bonus point claims.

crm_rows.title: Olivia Rodrigo pink Baja Blast and festival activation
crm_rows.what_happening: Taco Bell launched the Olivia Rodrigo pink Baja Blast in select California, Las Vegas and Texas locations before a Sept 24 nationwide release. It ran an activation at her Daisy Chain Fields festival, serving samples and giving out merch.
crm_rows.why_flowcode_fits: Festival sampling and limited-edition merch reach fans who likely stay unidentified. A code can capture them and send them to the drink and the app.
crm_rows.suggested_play: Your Olivia Rodrigo 'You Seem Pretty Pink for a Baja Blast' drink launched in select markets and went nationwide on Sept 24, with an activation at her Daisy Chain Fields festival. You likely cannot tell how many sample recipients or merch holders became customers. Put Flowcodes on sample cups, merch and ambassador signage that open a FlowHub with a Rewards sign-up, the nearest store and the app. You would see scans by event and by market and who signed up. Which part of the festival activation do you measure today?
crm_rows.would_measure: Scans by event, merch and cup, Rewards sign-ups, and drink-related store visits by market.

crm_rows.title: 2016 Decades Menu: link the Vine spot, Divine app and Tuesday Drop merch
crm_rows.what_happening: Taco Bell launched a 2016-themed Decades Menu with a Vine-inspired spot, a partnership with the Divine app, and exclusive Tuesday Drop merch (Anti Social Social Club, Camp Snap) plus an in-app scavenger hunt from Aug 25 to Sept 14.
crm_rows.why_flowcode_fits: The campaign spreads across TV, a partner app and Rewards. One code can send people to a single hub that routes them to the right place and shows which route worked.
crm_rows.suggested_play: Your 2016 Decades Menu launched on Aug 27 with a Vine-style spot, the Divine app partnership and a Rewards scavenger hunt running to Sept 14. You likely cannot see how many people moved from the spot to the app hunt or the Divine tie-in. Put a Flowcode on the spot and a branded FlowURL in partner posts that open a FlowHub linking to the Rewards app hunt, the merch drop and Divine. You would see which touchpoint drove Rewards activity during the hunt. How do you tie your TV spots to in-app scavenger hunt participation today?
crm_rows.would_measure: Scans and clicks by source, Rewards app opens and hunt participation, and merch drop entries.

crm_rows.title: Birmingham New Street opening: scan-to-claim free taco and prize wheel
crm_rows.what_happening: Taco Bell opened a station restaurant at Birmingham New Street with a free Crunchy Taco for the first 100 customers and a prize wheel for merch.
crm_rows.why_flowcode_fits: A promo built on a queue and a wheel can capture each participant's details through a scan.
crm_rows.suggested_play: Your Birmingham New Street station restaurant opened with a free Crunchy Taco for the first 100 customers and a prize wheel for merch. You likely have no record of who took part or whether they return. Put a Flowcode on the queue signage and prize wheel that opens a FlowHub where people claim their prize, join Rewards and see store hours. You would get an opted-in list and a count of first-day visitors. How do you capture contact details from new store openings today?
crm_rows.would_measure: Scans, sign-ups, prize claims and return visits after opening day.

crm_rows.title: Taco Bell grocery line: on-pack codes for Cravings Kits, sauces and seasonings
crm_rows.what_happening: Taco Bell Home Originals products (Cravings Kits, seasonings, sauces, bottled hot sauces with Kraft Heinz) are sold at Walmart, BJ's, Sam's Club and other grocers. The line's packaging was redesigned to tie back to the restaurant brand.
crm_rows.why_flowcode_fits: Grocery sales are anonymous to Taco Bell. An on-pack code can link shoppers to the restaurant app and capture who they are.
crm_rows.suggested_play: Your Cravings Kits, seasonings and hot sauces are sold at Walmart, BJ's, Sam's Club and other grocers, and the Home Originals packaging was redesigned to echo the restaurant brand. You likely cannot see who buys these at the grocery shelf or whether they come to your restaurants. Put a GS1 Digital Link-compliant Flowcode on the packs that opens a FlowHub with recipes, a Rewards sign-up and an offer for the restaurant. You would see scans by product and retailer and new Rewards members from grocery shoppers. Flowcode result: Lunchables saw a 22% sales lift and 50% campaign conversion from playable packaging. Who owns the link between grocery and Rewards on your team?
crm_rows.would_measure: Scans by product and retailer, Rewards sign-ups from grocery packs, and restaurant offer redemptions.

crm_rows.title: College of Idaho basketball sponsorship: codes on jerseys and courtside barriers
crm_rows.what_happening: Taco Bell is a multi-year sponsor of College of Idaho women's basketball with its logo on jerseys, and it sponsors the purple barriers in front of the student section at men's and women's home games.
crm_rows.why_flowcode_fits: Sponsor logos in a crowd give little measurable return. A scannable code on the barriers could capture student sign-ups and show the value.
crm_rows.suggested_play: Your College of Idaho deal puts the Taco Bell logo on women's basketball jerseys and on the purple barriers in front of the student section. You likely cannot measure what fans do after seeing the logos. Add a Flowcode to the barriers and arena screens that opens a FlowHub with a Rewards sign-up and a game-night offer. You would see scans per game and who joined. How do you currently show the return on local sponsorships like this?
crm_rows.would_measure: Scans per game and placement, Rewards sign-ups, and offer redemptions near campus.

crm_rows.title: Live Más Student Section: capture the 500 students
crm_rows.what_happening: Taco Bell runs a Live Más Student Section for 500 students at the CFP National Championship Tailgate, built with agencies Etzel and Star. It includes photo ops, games and free food trucks.
crm_rows.why_flowcode_fits: A branded on-site event with photo ops and games is a natural place for a scan-to-join code. Without one, the contact details of students who attend likely stay with the event team.
crm_rows.suggested_play: Your Live Más Student Section at the CFP Championship Tailgate hosts 500 students each year, with photo ops, games and food trucks. You likely have few ways to follow up with those students after the event. Put Flowcodes on the photo-op signage, game stations and food truck windows that open a FlowHub with a Rewards sign-up, an app download and an offer for the next visit. Give each station its own code. You would get sign-ups and scans by station and a list of opted-in students you can reach later. Flowcode result: NFL Shop made $25k in revenue and 10k connections in 60 seconds. What do you do today to stay in touch with the students after the tailgate?
crm_rows.would_measure: Scans per station, Rewards sign-ups, app installs, and later redemption of the follow-up offer.
